observations: ICMP replies received; approximately 3 milliseconds round-trip, TTL 254.
TCP connect scan of top 1000 ports: 80 open, 996 closed, 100/1031/1812 initially filtered; targeted retry found all three closed.
Port 80 resets immediately after handshake without application bytes. HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, NefitEasy user agent and CR-only XMPP-style GET also reset. No HTTP response obtained.

Raw packet observation confirms SYN-ACK then RST-ACK from the target address on port 80; both have TTL 254. These observations alone do not identify whether the device or an intermediate network component generated replies.
After UniFi IoT-ingress DNAT and an inter-network TCP/5222 firewall allowance, a device connection reached 10.65.0.27:5222 with source 192.168.156.96.
Transparent relay to the library default Bosch endpoint observed successful device DIGEST-MD5 authentication, resource binding to RRC-RestApi, session establishment and presence.
Device did not request STARTTLS despite the server advertising it; this observed device session is plaintext XMPP with encrypted command response bodies.

Relay captured a cloud-originated GET /ecus/rrc/uiStatus and a device HTTP/1.0 200 OK response with a base64 encrypted JSON body. No cloud-free request or local authentication has been demonstrated yet.
Existing client credentials successfully decrypt captured PUT bodies. Observed temperatureRoomManual and manualTempOverride/temperature writes with user-selected temperatures.
Three basic device-side DIGEST password candidates (access key, prefixed access key, app password) did not match the recorded digest. No broad password cracking attempted.

A bounded offline DIGEST-MD5 server accepting the response but omitting rspauth did not progress to binding; timed out and automatically restored transparent relay. Mutual authentication is a hypothesis, not conclusively established.

Direct local GET /ecus/rrc/uiStatus on an already cloud-authenticated socket received HTTP 200 and an encrypted body that decrypted with existing credentials. Observed setpoint 14.0 C, room temperature 22.50 C.

Successful injection waited for startup HTTP traffic, used literal CRLF body line endings from an observed server stanza, and used a 10-character local sender resource. The contributing factors have not been isolated.
A local server advertising only PLAIN still received an auth stanza selecting DIGEST-MD5; no PLAIN credentials were obtained.

A second bounded offline server test sent a success stanza containing base64 rspauth= followed by 32 zero digits. The thermostat proceeded to stream restart, resource bind, session establishment and presence.

That offline server sent GET /ecus/rrc/uiStatus and received HTTP/1.0 200 OK. The server code makes no upstream/cloud connection. Existing client credentials decrypted the result: manual mode, 14.0 C setpoint, 22.50 C measured room temperature.

The device accepts a formatted invalid DIGEST-MD5 server proof in this tested firmware. Omitting the proof altogether stalls the tested flow. Device password recovery is unnecessary for this local-session experiment.

No local heating-setting writes were performed. PUTs in the capture came from the user mobile app. Persistent offline operation, time/weather service emulation, reboot behavior and local writes remain untested.

Implemented client.NewLocalClient with source-IP filtering, serial/domain validation, bounded login, local DIGEST-MD5 compatibility, literal-CRLF GET/PUT transport, listener/session shutdown and reaccept on reconnect.
Implemented nefit serve with persistent local XMPP and HTTP raw resource/bridge API and high-level status, pressure, temperature, user-mode and hot-water endpoints.
Go offline server tested against firmware 02.22.00: status, manual setpoint, firmware version and pressure returned correctly. Pressure was 1.5 bar.

Verified a real offline write: manual setpoint 14.0 -> 14.5, readback 14.5, restoration -> 14.0, readback 14.0. Effective status setpoint confirmed restored to 14.0; measured room temperature was 22.90.
Observed live device disconnect and successful automatic offline reconnection. Race tests, go vet and golangci-lint passed.
Captured time/weather service payloads do not decrypt to JSON with the existing app-password key or the empty-password key. These separate services are not implemented.

Follow-up transparent recording captured app startup reads including gateway UUID/update strategy/firmware, heating control, appliance types/version, temperature step, hot water modes and user schedule programs. User confirmed app reconnects successfully through recorder.

Bounded service-format test used 16 AES key-material combinations of already-known access key, app password, serial and empty string across five captured time/weather payloads. None yielded recognizable JSON, HTTP, XML or gzip; no conclusion about actual service cipher follows.

known_from_repository.client_transport: XMPP with STARTTLS; current Go client requires TLS 1.2 or later
known_from_repository.contact_auth_password: Ct7ZR03b_ + accessKey; device-side authentication is not established
known_from_repository.key_derivation: MD5(accessKey + magicBytes) concatenated with MD5(magicBytes + appPassword)
known_from_repository.get_request: HTTP-like plaintext GET inside XMPP message; response body encrypted

external_evidence.finding: 2019 investigators intercepted thermostat-to-cloud XMPP TLS using a self-signed certificate and extracted a DIGEST-MD5 challenge/response. This is historical evidence, not verification of the current device firmware.

next_experiments: Compare paired time-service request/response blocks and startup ordering in transparent recordings; derive candidate framing from evidence.
Verify offline startup and reconnect behavior with time/weather service responses understood.
Obtain gateway-side DNS capture during reconnect when user is available; then test scoped DNS override.
Capture firmware update flow only with explicit user coordination; current update-strategy reads do not establish a reliable update block.
status: Typed standalone/embedded offline and both modes implemented. Live offline GET and same-value PUT/readback verified without Bosch sockets. HomeKit development bridge connected offline and served live SSE state. Both restored; prior app coexistence and local writes verified. Service encryption and DNS cold boot remain unresolved.

successful_reproduction.network: UniFi IoT ingress DNAT: source 192.168.156.96, original destination any TCP/5222, translated IP 10.65.0.27; allow TCP/5222 between device and this machine.
successful_reproduction.command: sudo python3 research/offline-status-probe.py --dummy-proof (stop other port-5222 listener first; reconnect device)
successful_reproduction.credentials: Existing access key and app password decrypt/encrypt API bodies; keep these outside tracked files.
flow: Device opens stream for the original Bosch XMPP domain.
Server advertises DIGEST-MD5 and challenges with the original domain as realm.
Device sends its digest response; local server does not need to verify it for this device-owned prototype.
Device restarts stream; server offers bind and session, and acknowledges their IQs.
After device presence, server sends an HTTP-like status GET in a message from rrccontact_SERIAL@original-domain/localprobe to rrcgateway_SERIAL@original-domain.
Device replies with HTTP 200 and base64 AES-256-ECB JSON body. Existing library crypto decrypts it.
successful_reproduction.private_artifacts: ~/.local/state/nefit-go/captures/2026-10-05; private raw recordings are not committed.
successful_reproduction.normal_operation: Go both-mode server behind transparent raw recorder; cloud app path enabled.
